recognize_zh: 新生兒周邊血液低倍視野中即可數到五顆有核紅血球（NRBC），並伴隨紅血球大小不一、多染性大紅血球及少數橢圓形或淚滴狀紅血球，顯示骨髓對溶血的強烈造血反應，符合 RhD 新生兒溶血症。
features: Increased circulating nucleated red cells (about five in this field) with dense round nuclei and polychromatophilic or orthochromatic cytoplasm
Anisocytosis with scattered large pale polychromatophilic red cells
Mild poikilocytosis with occasional elliptocytes and teardrop forms
Few spherocytes; most red cells retain central pallor
One segmented neutrophil and scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows increased numbers of nucleated red blood cells, with approximately five normoblasts in this field, together with a segmented neutrophil. The red cells show anisocytosis with scattered large polychromatophilic cells and mild poikilocytosis including occasional elliptocytes and teardrop forms, while spherocytes are not prominent. Platelets appear adequate. Findings indicate marked erythropoietic response with circulating normoblasts and are consistent with hemolytic disease of the newborn, such as RhD alloimmunization, in the appropriate clinical setting with a positive direct antiglobulin test.

ddx.dx: ABO hemolytic disease of the newborn
ddx.vs: ABO HDN is usually milder with numerous microspherocytes and fewer NRBCs, whereas RhD HDN shows more marked erythroblastosis with few spherocytes.
Normal neonates may have a few NRBCs in the first day, but not with anemia, marked polychromasia and a positive DAT.
Hypoxia and congenital infection also increase NRBCs, but they are DAT negative and lack alloantibody evidence.
TAM shows circulating megakaryoblasts and blasts in a newborn with trisomy 21, rather than a predominantly erythroid response.
